correctness.rationale: Parameterizing every planar orthonormal basis reduces the source invariant to \(F(\theta)=(\cos\theta+a\sin\theta)^{-2}+(\cos\theta-b\sin\theta)^{-2}\). The exact derivative \(F'(0)=2(b-a)\) makes every nonsymmetric matrix strictly subsharp. For \(a=b=q\), the substitution \(u=\tan^2\theta\) gives \(F=2(1+u)(1+q^2u)/(1-q^2u)^2\), whose derivative has a strictly positive numerator and the stated sign change across the pole. This proves the exact minimum \(2/\max\{1,q^2\}\) and the PSD equality locus. The argument includes \(q=0\), \(|q|=1\), orientation reversal, and vanishing-denominator boundaries.

value.rationale: The basis minimization is the central quantitative device in a new two-page proof of Ball's theorem, and the source uses only the coarse universal bound. The planar result identifies exactly when that bound is genuinely tight and when the same proof automatically yields a strict gain. The equality set is not arbitrary: it coincides exactly with the positive-semidefinite correlation matrices that underlie the classical Gram/Bang mechanism. This gives a structural bridge between the new variational proof and the classical matrix proof, while the exact symmetric formula quantifies the transition into the indefinite regime.
